question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.7
solution:
The correct answer is option 3), i.e., 'incidence.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the meaning of the words given in the options: 

 
 
 

 Word
 Meaning
 
 
 
 

 urgency
 the quality of being very important and needing attention immediately. (बहुत महत्वपूर्ण होने और तुरंत ध्यान देने की गुणवत्ता)
 
 

 deliverance
 the state of being saved from a painful or bad experience. (दर्दनाक या बुरे अनुभव से बचाए जाने की अवस्था या भाव)
 
 

 incidence
 an event, or the rate at which something happens. (एक घटना, या वह दर जिस पर कुछ होता है)
 
 

 frequency
 the number of times something happens within a particular period. (किसी विशेष अवधि के भीतर कितनी बार कुछ होता है)
 
 
 
 

 
• Let's look at the sentence: "...1 in 22 births to the Yoruba people** produces** twins, identical or fraternal, which is a much higher **__________** than anywhere else in the world."
 
• We can say that the implied meaning of the sentence is 1 in 22 births to the Yoruba people are twins, and the rate of such an **unusual event** is higher than in any other place.
 
• According to the above-mentioned points, the most appropriate option to fill in the blank is "incidence" to make the sentence meaningfully correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

​

Complete passage:__ In August every year, thousands of twins descend on a town in Ohio called Twinsburg, named by identical twin brothers 1. nearly two centuries ago. The Twins Days Festival is a three-day 2. event consisting of talent shows and look-alike 3. contests that have become one of the world's 4. largest gatherings of twins. There have been 5. similar festivals in Nigeria, a country where 1 in 22 births to the Yoruba people 6. produces twins, identical or fraternal, which is a much higher 7. incidence than anywhere else in the world. This has been 8. attributed to the eating of yams, but the theory is 9. disputed. Biomedical researchers attend these events, regarding them as a 10. precious opportunity to conduct surveys and experiments.
